4. For the sake of brevity, the two victims shall mention as V1 and V2.

sentences.text: PROSECUTION STORY:
5. The FIR was instituted by the informant stating that his two daughters aged about 16 years and 12 years were missing since 20.09.2023 at about 08:00 pm, when they had gone to ease themselves out.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT:
6. The applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case due to ulterior motive.
He has nothing to do with the said offence as alleged in the FIR.
7. The applicant is not named in the FIR.
8. The FIR itself is delayed by about two days and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
9. The name of the applicant has come up in the statements of the victims V1 and V2 recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
The said statements are self-contradictory and inconsistent to each other.

10. The statement of victim V1 indicates that she is a consenting party as she had subsequently gone to the house of the applicant, which stands fortified by the fact that the Investigating Officer has noted out in the case diary that victim V1 has gone to the house of the applicant and has refused to leave the said house despite being persisted.

11. The victim V2 by her physical appearance seems to be major although as per ossification test report her age has come out to be 17 years and the age of the elder one V1 shall naturally be more than her.
12. It is pertinent to mention that the victim V1 has plainly refused to get herself ossification test conducted, as such, presumption may be raised that she was major.

13. In the statement of the victim V2 recorded by the doctor at the time of her medical examination,
it has come up that it was the victim V1, who was the friend of the applicant and was responsible for the offence committed with her also.
14.
The medical examination report of victim V2 does not indicate any violence to her.
15. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.

16. The applicant is languishing in jail since 20.10.2023, having no criminal history to his credit,
deserves to be released on bail.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and shall cooperate with trial.

sentences.text: The bail application has been opposed on the ground that the applicant has misused his clout as he has taken away two minor girls all the way to Delhi and ravished them, as such, he is not entitled for bail.

CONCLUSION:
18. 13.
The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

19. A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been reiterated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
20.

sentences.text: Reiterating the aforesaid view, the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595, has again emphasized that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

sentences.text:
It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that "bail is a rule and jail is an exception".
21.
Learned AGA could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
22. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned AGA.

23. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, taking into consideration that the FIR is delayed, the victim V1 has refused her medical examination as well as her radiological examination and also the fact that the victim V2 has come out to be aged about 17 years, pending trial and considering the complicity of accused, severity of punishment, at this stage, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

24. Let the applicant- Daya Shankar, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.

sentences.text: (i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.

(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
25. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

26. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
